Container.Name: GameHueFlicker
Container.Overview:
Drives Philips Hue lights with the flicker patterns of classic shooters, through a small web UI that several people on your network can use at once.
Twenty games' worth of presets. Quake's lightstyle table is here verbatim from id Software's released source, shared with Quake II, Half-Life and Source which ship it unchanged, plus hand-authored takes on the light effects of DOOM, Heretic, Hexen, Descent, Marathon, Rise of the Triad, Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Shadow Warrior, Thief, System Shock 2, Doom 3, Quake 4 and Unreal. Every preset is named after the game it comes from and carries the speed it was written for, so picking one brings its timing with it.
Write your own patterns too, and share them: export yours to a small JSON file to send to someone, or import one they sent you.
Talks directly to your Hue Bridge over the local API - no Philips cloud account needed. Pick lights, pattern, speed, brightness range and colour, and change any of it while the lights are still running. Build entertainment areas from the console and stream a whole set at once, copying the rooms you already set up in the Hue app if you like, write your own a-z lightstyle strings, and watch a live waveform of what each light is doing.
The console reads each bulb's colour and brightness before it starts, and puts it back when the flicker stops - even if the container was restarted mid-run.
For an entertainment area set up in the Hue app, it can stream instead. The ordinary path spends one HTTP command per light out of a budget of about ten a second, so seven bulbs flicker at barely 1 Hz each; streaming sends one frame holding the whole area, so the speed stops being divided and every light changes together at up to 25 Hz. Streaming needs a pairing that included a streaming key, so a console set up before this feature has to pair again - the panel says so when that applies.
Everything is configured in the web UI, including the optional console password and the bridge send-rate cap - there are no environment variables to set here.
First run: open the WebUI, either auto-discover your bridge or type its IP, then press the physical link button on the bridge and hit Pair within 30 seconds.
If discovery or pairing fails on the default bridge network, switch Network Type to Host and try again.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the flicker console web UI. Defaults to 26000 (Quake's own port) to stay clear of the usual 8080 crowd.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Holds config.json: your bridge pairing, saved custom patterns, console password and settings. Keep this mapped or you will have to re-pair with the bridge after every update.
